changes: - Got all the basics set up. There's currently just a screen that shows an image of a popplio sprite. It's amazing
- Working on making the map on screen able to show arbitrary tiles.

- The neat thing about how I'm handling the tiles is that they're being placed on a 2d plane via uvs, and are not simply 1000 very carefully placed squares. It's all one big square cut up into pieces. The advantage here is that updating which tile something displays is easy, as well as that rendering 1 quad is faster than 1000 quads.
- It took some doing, but I made a function that lets me update an arbitrary tile to have an arbitrary value.
- Now I can also rotate tiles if I feel like it
- Working on a separate page to help with developing maps. It can display them in simpler 2d and help show what I'm making without so much trial and error.
- Made a pretty basic little test map. It's still completely 2d but I can add stuff soon.
- Honestly I'm pretty happy with the little bit of story I've got written down so far. It's not in the game yet, but I have a plan for the first few levels.
- The game now loads maps from a file, and as usual I've left it open to load other stuff later if somebody else makes a campaign.
- Created a very rough map for the tutorial level to take place on.
- I can now place props onto the map. They're just model files, but I could add any model I like. I'm using it for trees right now in the forest.
- Added a really neat shader that makes the map fade at the edges!
- Put a good amount of work into getting a damn character to exist on the map. There's a lot to think about and prepare for.
- Characters can now use sprite sheets to display multiple different sprites.
- Because my terrain sprites are smaller than my pokemon sprites, now the map can be shrunk/scaled.
- Made characters facing towards the camera work better.
- Added a bucket tool to my little map making program. Neat
- Added a bunch of trees to the map I'm working on.
- The camera now automatically focuses on the player
- The first scene needs a stufful in it, and I added it.
- Lots of work towards starting to make cutscenes work. I've done this a few times already, surely it can't be that bad in 3d. Right?
- The game now has a separate map storing the actual terrain information of the map. This includes information about which tiles each tile is connected to.
- Working on pathfinding. Not that hard honestly. It'll get a lot harder once there's a big pokemon. That's a later problem.
- Cutscenes can now tell characters to move to different tiles.
- Made a mugshot sprite for popplio. Mugshot sprites are the big ones that are used in dialogue and on profile screens.
- Working on the system for displaying characters' mugshots in the correct places during dialogue. As usual, I am making this too hard on myself by allowing arbitrary resolutions.

- Starting to work on how to create the box that the words actually go in during dialogue. I'm happy with how crisp the edges are on the characters, and I hope to do the same thing for the talk box, as I'm calling it.
